f'(\theta)=i e^{i\theta}(1+e^{i\theta})^2,
\]
so
\[
|f'(\theta)|=|1+e^{i\theta}|^2=4\cos^2(\theta/2).
\]
The curve has a self-intersection and a cusp, but its full trace forms the boundary of the enclosed region, so the perimeter is the total arc length:
\[
\int_0^{2\pi}4\cos^2(\theta/2)\,d\theta
=2\int_0^{2\pi}(1+\cos\theta)\,d\theta=4\pi.
\]

FINAL: \(4\pi\)

Using the falling-factorial expansion, the maximum is known/derived as
\[
k(n,p)=n+v_p(n!).
\]
Indeed, \(x^{\underline{pn}}\) has \(x^n\)-coefficient \(\equiv (-1)^n\not\equiv 0\pmod p\) and \(v_p((pn)!)=n+v_p(n!)\), while any nonzero coefficient from \(x^{\underline{ap+r}}\) forces \(a\le n\), giving \(v_p((ap+r)!)\le n+v_p(n!)\).

For \(p=11\), \(v_{11}(n!)=1\) for \(11\le n\le 15\), so
\[
k(n,11)=n+1: \quad 12,13,14,15,16 \quad \text{sum }70.
\]
For \(p=13\),
\[
v_{13}(n!)=
\begin{cases}
0,& n=11,12,\\
1,& n=13,14,15,
\end{cases}
\]
so
\[
k(11,13)=11,\quad k(12,13)=12,\quad k(13,13)=14,\quad k(14,13)=15,\quad k(15,13)=16,
\]
sum \(68\).

Total \(70+68=138\).

FINAL: 138

We count the tilings and proper 3-colorings together.

- There are \(18\) L-triomino tilings of the \(4\times 6\) rectangle.
- \(16\) of these are formed by concatenating two \(4\times 3\) tilings.
- The remaining \(2\) are the two “interlocking” exceptional tilings.

For the \(16\) concatenated tilings, summing the proper 3-colorings gives \(1152\).
For the \(2\) exceptional tilings, each has \(6\) valid colorings, giving \(12\).

Total:
\[
1152+12=1164.
\]

FINAL: 1164
